_about: 카드별 그림 지시(영어). 카드 이름만으로 모습이 분명하지 않거나 꼭 들어가야 할 것이 있을 때 카드 ID로 적는다. 스페셜 · 유니크는 모두 적는다(새로 만들 때도). build_prompts.js가 프롬프트의 'Art direction' 줄로 넣는다.
SP-B1: A colossal being of living fire who swallowed the sleeping giant Dormak's heart-fire whole — one of a kind: a towering, majestic titan of cracked black basalt and flowing magma, taller than Fortan's chimneys and gun bastions, which look like toys at his feet. In his open chest Dormak's heart-fire blazes like a furnace sun behind ribs of cooling rock, and molten light pours from his eyes and mouth. One arm is raised and a cannon-blast of fire erupts from his palm — each breath he exhales is a whole battery's volley — while pillars of smoke and ash rise around his head like a crown. Tiny gunners kneel on the bastion walls below, lit by his glow, not daring to speak his name. Behind him the volcano-chest of the giant Dormak splits open across the whole sky. Terrible grandeur, not a monster.
SP-B2: The heart is the focus: an enormous iron heart forged from the giant Sorgrim's sinew-ore — dark adamant plates, brass valves and pistons like arteries, molten forge-light pulsing through its seams — beating at the centre of the image, larger than a forge furnace. The one who swallowed it is a colossal armoured presence that is only partly seen: his vast shape is veiled in steam, shadow and forge smoke and revealed only in glimpses — the edge of a riveted iron shoulder like a cliff, a giant gauntleted hand resting on an anvil the size of a house, two eyes glowing high above in the darkness. Hundreds of chains and pipes run from the heart up into the hidden body; let the viewer imagine the full titan from these clues. Around it stretches the underground forge-cathedral of Durkheim; rows of golems, tiny by comparison, kneel facing the heart, their own chest-lights waking in rhythm with its beat, the oldest and most patched golem kneeling closest. He ascended without any god: instead of a halo, slowly turning rings of gears and golden runes circle the heart.
SP-B3: The Seventh: an automaton prototype that one day began to think. An elegant copper-and-glass body with seven glowing lightning nodes (no numerals), a lightning brain visible inside a glass dome head, one hand raised in wonder at a spark it made itself. Tiny scholars look up at it from its feet.
SP-G1: Karno Ashmane: a colossal duel-titan of living stone and ash, one of a kind. A towering warrior body of cracked dark granite and basalt with glowing ochre-orange magma seams, every one of his hundred duel scars a molten crack; a vast mane of grey ash and drifting embers streams from his head and shoulders like a volcanic plume (the 'ash mane'); fists like boulders bound in ancient leather straps; his face is a stern, noble mask of stone with burning eyes. He stands in a stone duel ring cracked into a crater, mid-stride and roaring a challenge, rock dust and embers exploding around his feet. Behind him the mountain-sized earth dragon Gorbas, forests on its back, lowers its great head to meet him eye to eye, as if for a hundred-and-first duel, while the standing stones and nomad camps of the Garun steppe lie tiny below and a trail of ash-grey smoke drifts across the plain behind him.
SP-G2: Lisiel Silvermoon, a walking forest that moves only on nights of the waxing moon — one of a kind: a tall being half figure and half tree, bark skin threaded with silver moonlit veins, branches for hair, ember-scarred bark with young green leaves regrowing from every scar, saplings sprouting wherever it steps. It once took a burning forest's fire into its own body and raised a thousand-year forest from the ashes in a single night. Silver moonlight mixed with green spore-light; the forest dragon Verdan's branch-antlers form a canopy above.
SP-G3: She Who Lulls the Sea: the oldest song remembered by the water dragon Marencia, given a body — one of a kind. A serene woman-shaped being whose body from the waist down and through her flowing hair is living, translucent water; her hands are joined as she sings, and her song spreads over the dark sea as glowing rings of light; a blade passing through her becomes only ripples. Far below, in the black trench, the faint glow of the sleeping giant Talakus's colossal heart slows to the rhythm of her song. Behind her the translucent serpentine body of Marencia coils through the sky like a river of light, forming a halo. Calm, sacred and vast.
SP-A1: Azra the Shadowless at the height of her ascension — a colossal, regal figure standing above the sunless canyon city of Noctar, so tall that its violet-lit spires reach only to her knees. Her great curved horns form a dark crown framed by a total eclipse that serves as her halo; a vast cloak of living night spills from her shoulders down the canyon walls like a waterfall of shadow. Every shadow in the city — of towers, bridges and kneeling figures — stretches and bends toward her like supplicants, yet she herself casts none: the ground beneath her feet is bright and bare, make the missing shadow unmistakable. Her face is serene and half-veiled by drifting shadow-silk, eyes glowing violet. A burning contract scroll floats beside her open hand, its blood seal glowing. Above her in the sky the faceless shadow king Morkas holds his scales, one pan weighed down by something veiled — what she gave. Calm, still, overwhelming power — not an action pose.
SP-A2: The First Knight of Solante, the first ever to swear an oath to the Mother of Dawn — a mythic champion: lifted by the goddess herself, vast wings of light bursting from his back, rising from one knee with his sword raised toward the dawn; where his blade is raised the night recoils and sunrise floods the sky. He is colossal: he kneels on the hills beyond the Dawn Citadel Elad, whose white walls and towers reach only to his knee, and the armies on its walls are tiny specks of light; each of his wings spans the whole horizon, and his face is lit high above the clouds.
SP-A3: Isaac who unravelled the stars, the first to read the star glyphs — a transcendent star-mage: he pulls threads of starlight down from the sky into an open book while a whole constellation unravels and re-weaves itself around him as abstract glyphs, and the sky obeys; silver hair and robes swept by star-wind. He is colossal: he stands among the clouds above Belumir's Needle, its tallest spires reaching only to his waist and tiny watchers on its lookout platforms looking up; the constellation he unravels covers the whole sky, and its threads of starlight fall into his book like rivers.
SR-A1: The greatsword of Hargan the Judge, drawn only once to punish a god: a colossal two-handed sword of dark adamant and gold, scales of judgment engraved on the blade, standing point-down in a cracked divine altar under a beam of judgment light.
SR-A2: The bow of Seren the Gatekeeper, who guards the edge of the world: a tall bow of pale silver and starlight, a nocked arrow of light drawn by no hand, aimed at a dark horizon where the world ends.
SR-A3: The quill of Ivel the Recorder: a great feather quill whose ink is ether light, writing glowing abstract strokes in the air that turn into tiny real scenes; an endless library fades behind it.
SR-B1: A furnace carved from one colossal rib bone of the sleeping giant Dormak: the curved ivory-black rib forms the body of a brazier, glowing heartfire roaring inside, flames leaping hungrily toward a burning ember on the ground, volcanic ash drifting.
SR-B2: The first armour of the sleeping giant Sorgrim: a huge breastplate made from a single giant rib segment fused with dark iron ore, a sword striking it bounces back with a shockwave of sparks thrown toward the attacker, iron ridge mountains behind.
SR-B3: A crackling heart fragment of the thunder giant Keraun, held in a brass-and-glass cage: the crystal heart pulses with branching blue lightning that races up the bearer's arm each time a spell circle flares nearby.
SR-G1: The broken fang of the earth dragon Gorvath: a massive cracked stone-and-bone fang strapped to a fist with hide cords, still stained, glowing amber veins pulsing as if it hungers, a fallen beast silhouette in the background.
SR-G2: The first antler of the forest dragon Verdan: a great branching antler of living wood, roots snaking from its base and drinking a faint green glow out of a thorned attacker toward the bearer, moss and leaves sprouting along its tines.
SR-G3: The chalice of the sea dragon Marencia's tears: a pearl-and-coral chalice overflowing with luminous blue water, a gentle tide spilling from its rim and flowing first toward a wounded figure, mist and soft light rising.
UN-B1: An old goblin artillery captain of Fortan with a long grey ear-tuft and a brass spyglass, commanding a battery of cannons; even while falling he grins and holds a lit fuse.
UN-B2: Bron's first golem: an old, patched, riveted golem carefully building a new small golem from the parts of fallen comrades with gentle hands.
UN-B3: The gnome researcher who once bottled the lightning spirit Zrak, holding the biggest empty jar while cracked empty jars around her refill with lightning.
UN-G1: The great chief of the Rockfang tribe: an enormous orc with a stone-fang necklace, howling as his warband charges out of the dust behind him.
UN-G2: An ancient treant keeper of thorns around the First Elder Tree; cut briars regrow from the roots all around him as he works.
UN-G3: A singer of the Spring Choir; her song spreads as glowing rings over the sea, and pale souls of the drowned ride the waves back toward the shore.
UN-A1: A demon writing his oath in his own blood with the edge of his blade; a crimson thread of the contract links his sword to his distant foe.
UN-A2: A radiant knight of Elad spreading her wings like a shield in front of her comrades, arrows breaking against the feathers.
UN-A3: A high-elf star-keeper archer on a lookout platform atop Belumir's Needle, bow half-drawn, reading abstract star glyphs carried on the wind before the enemy's spells arrive.
UN-B1-7: A goblin gunner planting embers scooped from Talakus's black blood-pulse into his shells; behind him the struck ground keeps burning in long lines.
UN-B2-7: Two huge gate golems of Durkheim bound together by one massive steel chain, moving as one wall.
UN-B3-7: A walking tower wound with Keraun's lightning; its magnetic field bends the air — coins, dice and metal debris spin in orbit around it.
UN-G1-7: An orc plunder-king wielding weapons he took from fallen foes, a heap of captured arms and banners at his feet.
UN-G2-7: An old treant with seed pouches hanging from his branches; wherever he walks after battle, a young forest springs up behind him.
UN-G3-7: A siren risen from Marencia's deep waters, singing on a rock; in the distance enemy soldiers turn their swords around against themselves.
UN-A1-7: A hooded wraith reaping souls with a great scythe; every soul he takes turns into a contract page fluttering into his hand.
UN-A2-7: A seraph priestess lifting the dawn light in both hands; fallen knights rise again behind her in the sunrise.
UN-A3-7: A night-elf spell-hunter archer: his arrow pierces a glowing enemy spell mid-air, and streams of foreign-coloured magic are pulled along the arrow into his bow and swallowed as light.
SG1-02: Finishing the staggering: on a rocky battlefield at dusk, several enemy soldiers (dark silhouettes) are already reeling and bloodied, barely standing after orc bites. A grim scarred orc walks down their line and drops each one with a short heavy chop of a stone-weighted fist; a thin ochre earth-glow pulses through the ground under all the wounded foes at once, as one last tremor finishes them. Mood: cold, decisive, no barrier or shield.
SG1-08: Fang counterattack: a small band of cornered Rockfist orcs, backs to a cliff wall, bracing together; their grey-green skin swells and toughens with a warm ochre earth-glow (gaining toughness), tusks bared in a snarl. The nearest orc bites back into the arm of an attacker who has just struck him — the attacker (dark silhouette) recoils, still alive but drained to a thread. Feeling: wounded but defiant, the pack bites back.
MC-01: Crouching wolves (v3.95): a pack of grey wolves and Rockfist orc hunters press flat to the ground in tall dry grass, fangs hidden, ears back, coiled and silent; facing them a line of enemy warriors (dark silhouettes) hesitate, weapons lowered and wavering, unsure where to strike. Low eye-level, tense calm before the spring, ochre dusk light.
SG1-03: Cornered fang (v3.95): a cornered pack of orcs and wolves surges forward as one at the foremost enemy (dark silhouette); in one sweep the bites tear away its weapon, then its armour plates, then reach its throat, and the leftover momentum already lunges at the next enemy behind. Motion-blurred fangs and claws, dust, brutal frontal composition.
MG-13: Bone breaker: an enemy warrior whose armour has already been torn and peeled away (broken plates and straps hanging off, bare chest and shoulders exposed, dark silhouette) is struck by a massive orc fist encased in rough stone; at the point of impact a sharp crack of ochre earth-light spreads like fractures through the body. Close, diagonal, brutal composition; the orc mostly out of frame, only the fist and forearm.
M2-1: An orc's tattooed fist: a huge grey-green orc fist, knuckles freshly tattooed with dark fang-shaped marks in ochre and black pigment, beside a bone tattoo needle and a small stone pigment bowl on dark leather; the tattoo glows faintly like it could tear through armour. Show the fist and tools, not a carved plate.
MC-03: Turned waterway: a lagoon channel whose current has suddenly reversed — a glowing blue-green river runs backwards across the battlefield, and the enemy line (dark silhouettes wading in it) is dragged and shuffled out of order, the heaviest armoured figures pushed to the front, nimble ones swept to the back. A merfolk priestess at the edge, small in frame, guides the reversed flow with one hand; a few drops of the water curl back to her as a soft glow. Show the reversal and the reordered line, not an explosion.
SG3-01: Illusion control: a Selenea priestess half-submerged in a moonlit lagoon sings; rings of pale light ripple out over the water. One enemy warrior (dark silhouette) on the far bank has lowered his weapon and walks into the water toward her side with dreamy, unseeing eyes, an illusory shimmer around his head, while his comrades behind reach after him too late. Mood: hypnotic, quiet, eerie — no explosion.
SG3-02: Water mirage: over a glittering lagoon a heat-haze of water-light bends the air. Two enemy soldiers (dark silhouettes) are caught in it and their reflections in the water are swapped — a hulking brute's reflection is a frail reed-thin figure and a slight one's reflection is a towering giant — the real bodies stagger as they take on their reflections. Shimmering, disorienting, no explosion.
NG2-3: Troll regeneration: two or three moss trolls in a dim forest clearing, fresh wounds on their bark-like grey-green skin knitting closed before our eyes — torn flesh pulling together with green fibres and tiny sprouting leaves, a gash on an arm already half healed, the trolls grinning and standing back up. Warm green life-glow from the wounds, a few fallen leaves; no fire anywhere (trolls fear fire).
SB1-05: Detonation: a goblin sapper behind a sandbag crouches and slams down a crude plunger; across the battlefield every enemy (dark silhouettes) that was already smouldering with embers bursts into flame at the same instant — a line of fiery explosions popping one after another, sparks and black smoke. Fortan chimneys in the haze behind. Chaotic, loud, joyful for the goblin.
SG2-01: Vine constrict: a thick thorny vine erupting from forest soil and wrapping a heavily armored warrior in steel plate, the vine wedging into the armor seams and squeezing — plates denting and bending, rivets popping. Dim green forest light, moss on the ground; the thicker the armor, the deeper the vine bites.
NG2-1: Burrowing roots: gnarled tree roots bursting up out of the earth around a line of armored soldiers, each root stabbing into the gaps of their armor (joints, visor slits, shoulder seams) while an unarmored figure stands untouched among them. Crumbling soil, flying clods, dark forest backdrop, cool green light.
MC-14: Armor-crushing entangle: countless vines sweeping across a battlefield and wrapping whole armored warriors, twisting and prying their breastplates and helmets off; loose armor plates sinking into a thick carpet of moss. Wide shot, dim forest, green-grey palette with a few glints of steel.
SA2-03: Prayer of Silence: a circle of robed celestial priests with folded white wings kneel in unison on a battlefield, heads bowed; a soft dome of pale golden quiet spreads from them, and inside it the glowing auras and weapon enchantments of the enemy front line fade out like snuffed candles. Still, hushed, gentle light.
NA2-1: Light of Redemption: a column of warm dawn light falls on a fierce enemy warrior; inside the beam his weapon slips from his hands and his hostile aura dissolves, and he stands calm with a plain kite shield like a young celestial shield apprentice. Soft gold rays, peaceful expression, dark battle behind.
SA2-07: Scales of Judgment: an enormous golden balance scale hangs in the sky above a battlefield; several enemy warriors bearing the same glowing mark are lifted onto one pan together and their weapons dim, each blade lightened by the weight of its bearer's rank. Solemn, radiant, ordered composition.
RS-A2-2: Light of Retribution: a celestial knight shelters behind spread white wings that catch a rain of enemy blades; the blocked strikes gather into a bright orb of light above the wings, then lance back as a single spear of radiance at the largest enemy. Defensive pose turning into a counterstrike.
SA2-02: Prayer of Endurance: two celestial shield-bearers stand braced at the front of a dark pre-dawn battlefield, small halos of light on their shields; each enemy blow that glances off leaves a tiny mote of gold light that drifts up and gathers into a faint growing glow on the eastern horizon behind them. Patient, enduring, the sky just starting to pale.
MA-10: Oath of the Martyr: a winged celestial knight falls to one knee mid-battle, sword slipping from his hand, his body dissolving into soft feathers of light; his last radiance flows sideways into two shield-shaped bubbles of light forming around the comrades standing on his left and right. Solemn, sacrificial, warm gold on a grey battlefield.
MA-14: Release of Dawn: a vast sunrise bursts over a battlefield all at once, a wall of gathered golden dawn light tearing across the horizon; the fiercest enemy champions in front, weapons raised, are struck first and thrown back blinded, while the leftover light settles gently over weary celestial soldiers and closes their wounds. Explosive radiance, long rays, triumphant turn.
IA2-1: Confiscated Obsidian Blade: a jagged black obsidian demon knife, its hilt wrapped in white linen strips inscribed with golden prayer script, lying on a celestial inquisitor's altar cloth; a thin dark red glint still clings to the edge.
SG2-05: Gathering the sap: four moss trolls in a dim forest clearing kneel with their palms pressed to the roots of one old tree-like troll; glowing amber-green sap streams out of their bodies along the roots into that one giant, which swells huge and bursting with life while the others slump thin, grey and exhausted. Warm sap glow against cool shadow.
SG2-08: Ancient trunk slam: a huge gnarled tree-troll rearing up with its roots torn from the ground and bringing its whole trunk-like body crashing down onto a line of enemy silhouettes; a shockwave of soil, splinters and moss bursting outward, the ground caving in. The troll's bark is cracking and drained grey after the blow. Low angle, dramatic, dim green forest light.
MG-04: Grudge strike: in the foreground a lone scarred Rockfist orc raises one huge fist high, the knuckles wrapped in strips of cloth and bone tokens taken from fallen orc brothers; faint ochre ghostly silhouettes of fallen orcs stand behind him like a shadow chorus, their glow flowing into the fist and making it heavier, as it is about to slam down on a dark enemy silhouette. Mood: grief turned into fury.
RS-G1-2: Blood oath: a circle of Rockfist orc warriors at night, each slicing an open palm with a bone knife and clasping hands together over a stone war-drum; their mixed blood glows deep red and runs as one thread from hand to hand down the line toward the warrior at the back. Solemn, tense, a vow before battle; dark crimson and ochre light.
RB1-1: Laying the powder kegs: a battered goblin crew, clearly losing — broken barricades and empty gaps along their own line — hurriedly rolls squat iron-banded powder kegs into every empty gap and slams them down; each keg's short fuse is already lit and sputtering orange sparks. In the background the enemy line (dark silhouettes) advances, unaware that the kegs face them. Mood: desperate, sly, a fuse-lit pause before the turn of the battle. Show the kegs being placed and lit, not an explosion.
SB1-08: Blowing the depot: a goblin sapper, ears flattened, slams a crude plunger while a whole row of powder kegs planted along the goblins' own line goes up at once in a chain of roaring fireballs; the blast throws the front enemy warriors (dark silhouettes) back in flames, and the goblins' own fighters nearby are knocked off their feet too, singed and smoking. Mood: reckless, devastating, a price paid on both sides.
MG-11: Overturned water-mirror: two enemy warriors (dark silhouettes) at the front stand at the edge of a still lagoon pool; in the water their reflections are upside down and wrong — the shield-bearer's reflection holds a raised blade, the swordsman's reflection hides behind a shield — and the real men falter, their stances flipping to match, dazed eyes glazed by the shimmer. A Selenea songstress, small in frame, touches the water's surface. Mood: eerie, mesmerising, quiet; no wave, no explosion.
SA3-06: Archers' Armory: the great wooden doors of the Storm Tower archers' armory swing open on a windy high-elf spire; racks of slender wind-wrapped longbows are handed out one by one to a mixed line of sky creatures — a harpy, a young griffin, an owl-like beast and a wind sylph — each now gripping its own bow, strings glinting, wind curling around the limbs; no arrows flying yet, the moment of arming.
NA3-3: Starlight Volley: a whole line of archers of the star banner — high elves, harpies and griffin riders, every one holding a bow — release at the same instant; their arrows turn into streaks of silver starlight that arc high and fall like a dense meteor shower over the entire enemy line below; the more bows, the thicker the star-rain, night-blue sky full of light trails.
MA-01: Blade of Dread (v3.95): two thin blades of living shadow, held by an elegant horned demon half-lost in violet smoke, slip past the two front enemy soldiers (dark silhouettes) without drawing blood — only cold black wisps cling where they brushed. The soldiers' hands tremble, their weapons sag, their eyes wide; faint whispering shadow-faces curl around their shoulders. Fear, not wounds: no gore, no spilled blood.
PS-A1-2: Plague Shackles (v3.95): a heavy rusted iron shackle with a blood-wax contract seal clamps around the wrist of the strongest enemy warrior (dark silhouette), dragging his weapon arm down; sickly green-violet rot seeps from the iron into his veins and spreads as creeping mould stains and drifting spores toward the comrades standing on either side of him. Corroded chain, sagging posture, a slow contagious dread.
MA-09: Hellfire (v3.95): the most heavily armoured enemy (a dark silhouette in thick plate and a tower shield) stands in front of an elegant horned demon who closes a clawed hand; the armour itself ignites from within — every plate glows red-hot and bursts into low, hungry violet-and-crimson hellfire, the thicker the plate the fiercer the flame, so his own armour burns him instead of protecting him. Black smoke rising, molten rivets dripping.
CS-A1: Possession of Silence (v3.95): left, a glowing enemy spell scroll is gagged shut by a ribbon of black smoke and goes dark. Centre, a huge, hale enemy champion (dark silhouette) stiffens as a small, frail, translucent ghost — the faint soul of the weakest little creature on the battlefield — slides into his chest; his mighty body suddenly looks as fragile as that ghost, knees buckling, eyes hollow. Violet underlight, whisper-thin smoke threads linking the two shapes. No blood.
RS-A1-3: Mind Domination (v3.95): an elegant horned demon contractor raises two fingers like a puppeteer; violet threads of light hook into the brow of an enemy warrior (dark silhouette, already marked by a faint curse sigil) whose eyes now glow the same violet; he has turned around on the battlefield and walks to stand at the back of the demon's own ranks, weapon pointing at his former comrades. Unsettling calm, closed-eye scales motif faint in the smoke above.
HA1-2: Fingertip Curse (v3.95 hand spell): an elegant pale clawed fingertip reaches through shadow smoke and lightly touches the top card of a fanned hand of enemy cards (blank card backs, no text); from that card a tiny shadow figure of a soldier crouches, trembling, wreathed in faint whispering black wisps — fear planted before it ever reaches the field.
HA1-3: Curse Contagion (v3.95 hand spell): a fanned hand of enemy cards (blank backs, no text) hovers in darkness; the two front cards are stained by creeping green-violet rot and mould spreading from a single blood-wax sigil, spores drifting toward the neighbouring cards. A slow, sickly infection crawling across the plans of the enemy.
US-A3-1: Contract of the New Moon (v3.95, now a Morkas's New Moon card): under a black new-moon sky above the canyon spires of Noctar, a long black-parchment contract unrolls in mid-air, sealed with blood-red wax and violet sigils; the enemy's name is inscribed on it in glowing blood ink (illegible, no real letters). Beneath it a fanned hand of enemy cards (blank backs) withers and greys like dying leaves, while one fresh card slides from the shadows into the caster's elegant clawed hand. Epic: violet light shafts, drifting ash, a faint faceless shadow king with balanced scales behind the moon.
RS-A2-1: Light of Judgment (v3.95): two winged celestial knights at the front of the line lower and plant their shields and strip open their breastplates, offering their own armour up; the light of that surrendered armour rises from them as two beams of white-gold radiance that merge into one great descending blade of judgment striking the first enemy (dark silhouette) — and, piercing through, carries on into the enemy behind. Solemn sacrifice turned into a strike; dawn sky.
PS-A2-1: Atonement in Another's Stead (v3.95): an enemy blade strikes the celestial soldier at the front of the line, but the wound appears instead on the winged comrade standing right behind him — a thread of golden light links the two, and the one behind is wrapped in a thin protective halo-ward, absorbing the blow with a calm, bowed head. Sacrificial, tender, warm gold on a grey battlefield.
SG1-01: Driving the Prey (v3.95): orc hunters with wolves and bone horns drive an enemy line (dark silhouettes) like a herd; the most wounded, limping and bleeding enemies are shoved and harried to the very front, the healthiest pushed to the back. Dust, bared fangs, the predator's eye picking the weakest.
SG2-02: Sprouting Armour (v3.95, formerly Bark Armour): a troll warrior's chest is plated with cracked old bark; from every crack fresh green shoots and young leaves are bursting out, curling over his wounds and knitting them closed as they grow. Mossy forest light, sap glistening, a quiet stubborn renewal rather than a hard shield.
SA3-02: Wind of Confusion (v3.95, formerly Wind Barrier): a twisting, disorienting gust hurled by a high-elf archer wraps the front enemy warrior (dark silhouette) in a spiral; his armour plates and his life-glow swap places in the whirl — steel pieces float out while a pale heartbeat light sinks inward — he staggers, vision warped, the air itself bent and crooked. Storm-grey and silver wind lines, no text.
SA3-05: Wind Recoil (v3.95, formerly Whirlwind Bulwark): two high-elf archers at the front stand braced inside a tight protective whirlwind that turns enemy blows aside; from within the cyclone they loose return arrows that slip straight through the gaps of the attackers' armour as if the plate were not there. Defensive and counter-striking at once; silver gusts, flying leaves, taut bowstrings.
PS-B3-1: Amplifier Circuit (v3.95, formerly Reverse Circuit): a goggled gnome engineer plugs two copper coils with glass tubes into the backpacks of the two allied soldiers at the front; thick blue-white lightning surges through the cables and makes the soldiers' own spells and weapons crackle twice as bright. Brass, copper wire, sparking capacitors, an excited grin; ally-boosting, not sabotage.
SG3-03: Veil of Water (v3.95): a thin, shimmering sheet of seawater rises like a translucent curtain in front of two merfolk warriors at the front; an enemy blade (dark silhouette) slices into it and is slowed and dulled, its edge blunted by the flowing water; a soft cleansing ripple washes dark wisps off the foremost warrior. No solid shield, no bubble dome — a gentle flowing veil.
MB-05: Ember Scatter (v3.95, formerly Burst Shell): a grinning goblin swings and flings an open sack of glowing coals; a spray of embers arcs through the smoky air and settles on the two front enemy soldiers (dark silhouettes), catching on their cloaks and straps as small hungry flames. Fortan chimneys in the haze; mischievous, not explosive.
NB1-3: Fire Wind (v3.95, formerly Mortar Barrage): a scorching wind born from Dormak's heart-fire roars across the enemy army (dark silhouettes); every soldier is licked by flames on cloaks and banners while the one at the very front is engulfed in a whirling pillar of fire. Heat haze, blowing sparks and ash, goblins on a bastion cheering in silhouette. Rare: ember particles and glowing rim light.
